questions.q: Where does imported invoice data land BEFORE it becomes a real Payables invoice?
options: Directly in the live invoice records
In the supplier's own system
In the General Ledger
In open interface (staging) tables
questions.explain: Imported data is staged in open interface tables first; it is not immediately a live invoice.

questions.q: What does the Import Payables Invoices process do?
options: Reads staged interface data and builds real invoices and invoice lines from it
Deletes duplicate suppliers
Automatically pays every staged invoice
Converts invoices into purchase orders
questions.explain: This process turns valid staged rows into actual Payables invoices, the same kind created manually elsewhere in this chapter.

questions.q: Why would an imported invoice row be rejected due to 'no valid supplier site'?
options: Because the invoice amount was too large
Because the import data doesn't resolve to a real supplier and site that Payables can attach the invoice to
Because the invoice date is in the future
Because the business classification expired
questions.explain: Without a resolvable supplier site, Payables has nowhere to attach the invoice, so the row is rejected.

questions.q: Which control from manual invoice entry also applies during import?
options: Business classification certification
Supplier merge irreversibility
Duplicate invoice number detection per supplier
Bank account masking
questions.explain: The same duplicate invoice number check applies to imported invoices, rejecting a repeat invoice number for the same supplier.

questions.q: A batch import creates 395 out of 400 submitted invoices. What should happen next?
options: The rejections report should be reviewed so the underlying issues with the other 5 can be fixed and reattempted
Nothing — the batch is complete since most succeeded
The 5 missing invoices are automatically retried the next day with no action needed
The entire batch of 400 should be deleted and re-entered manually
questions.explain: Rejected rows don't just disappear safely — the rejections report must be checked and the underlying data corrected before those invoices get created.
